angle: TikTok retention. The first frame has to stop the scroll, the video has to read with the sound off, it has to loop without a visible seam, and nothing vital can sit under TikTok's buttons. The top 12% and bottom 20% stay clear, and so does x>960 between y 900 and 1536, where the like/comment/share rail sits. Two findings from reading piano.js. First, CC64 is already wired (onMidiMessage -> setSustain) and the trails already have a dim pedal tail. What washed out Daniel's playing is additive blending plus bloom: octave doublings and pedal tails all stack at their own key x. So both presets swap the 88 additive trails for a fixed geometry budget. Octaves merge per pitch class using max, not sum, so brightness can never build up. Second, the render loop already runs on requestAnimationFrame, so it draws at the monitor's native rate, and REC is already paced to 60 fps. The only framerate rule a new preset needs is to be time-based, never frame-based. Both presets share some scaffolding: a scheme registry, a scene rendered before bloom, a first-hit hook, a REC loop seam, and a lens shift that lifts the key fronts above y 1520. That is spelled out in scheme 1's build sketch.

schemes.name: Prism
schemes.pitch: Every key you press shoots light through a prism into twelve rainbow columns. Octaves stack into one clean bar, and a chord type makes the same barcode in any key, just slid sideways.
schemes.visuals:
LAYOUT 1080x1920:
- y 0-230: empty.
- Chord label: reuse drawLabel at cy 350, size 150, with the note-name row around y 470.
- History field: x 120-940, y 540-1180. 12 lanes, each about 68px wide with 8px gaps and rounded ends.
- Left gutter, x 16-112: scrolling chord tags, and a pedal bracket at x 108.
- Ray band: y 1180-1330.
- Keyboard: tune the lens shift so the key fronts end at or above y 1520.
- Below y 1536: floor reflection only.
- Right of x 960: decoration only.

LANE ORDER: circle of fifths, rotated so the guessed key's 7 notes fill lanes 3-9 (tonic on lane 4). The 5 notes outside the key sit at the edges (lanes 10, 11, 0, 1, 2). noteLch already sets hue by fifths, so the lanes read left to right as a smooth rainbow, and out-of-key notes light up at the edges.

REST / THUMBNAIL: lane guides at 6% alpha in their own colours. A letter under each lane at y 1195 (26px, 55% alpha); the tonic's letter at 85% with a small dot. No idle motion.

NOTE-ON:
- A ribbon ray fires in 120 ms from the key's projected rail point to the bottom of its lane. It is a cubic Bezier in the note colour, 6px at the key widening to lane width.
- A bright cap row (onset flash) appears at the bottom of the lane.
- The lane core fills at brightness 0.55 + 0.45*vel.
- The key dips and glows as it does today. Sparks drop to 30% of today's count, at the ray origin only.

HELD: a solid bar climbs the lane as the history scrolls at about 200 px/s (140 rows/s, about 3.7 s visible). The bar has a centre highlight. The top 90px of the field fades out beneath the label.

NOTE-OFF (pedal up): the ray pulls back down in 90 ms, and the bar ends in a rounded cap on that row.

SUSTAIN (CC64):
- While the pedal is down, a 2px gold line grows at x 108, with a 10px tick at each press and release, like the printed 'Ped.' bracket.
- A 1px gold hairline (alpha 0.22) crosses every lane on the pedal-down row.
- A note that is released but still pedalled carries on as a hollow lane: edge strokes plus an 18% fill, fading with tau 1.1 s. Its ray thins to 2px at 35% alpha.
- On pedal-up, the hollow segments stop with a flat cut, so the history shows exactly where he cleared.

CHORD CHANGE (when overlay.pop fires):
- A white hairline (alpha 0.25) crosses the lanes on that row.
- A chord tag sprite (e.g. 'Fmaj9', 30px semi-condensed, INK at 80%) appears in the gutter at the bottom of the field and scrolls up with its row, fading out in the top 20%. The history becomes a scrolling lead sheet.
- The big label pops as it does today.

KEY CHANGE: only after at least 1.2 s of silence and a confident new key (r >= 0.7, two estimates in a row agree). The lanes slide sideways to the new order over 700 ms, ease-in-out. Columns that wrap round fade at the edges.

HOOK: on the first note-on after REC starts, or after 3 s of silence:
- bloom.strength jumps from 0.45 to 0.95 and decays with tau 0.25 s.
- The camera pushes in 2.5% (cam.span) and eases back over 0.4 s.
- The lane guides flash to 20% for 150 ms.
It is one eased event, not per-frame noise.

16:9: lanes at x 1180-1860; the label stays on the left as today.
schemes.theory_value:
- Fifths order turns harmony into distance. Chords in the key sit as tight clusters in the centre lanes. A major scale is 7 neighbouring lanes and a pentatonic scale is 5.
- Borrowed and chromatic notes (bVII or iv in a major key, blue notes) light the edge lanes, so Daniel can see which exact note gives a chord its 'magic'.
- A chord type is a spacing pattern. In lane order a major triad is C G ... E, gaps +1 then +3; a minor triad is Eb ... C G, gaps +3 then +1. Major and minor read as mirror-image barcodes.
- Merging octaves teaches pitch class versus voicing: the lane is the note's name, the keyboard is where he voiced it.
- Pedal brackets and hollow tails show harmonic blur. Where two chords' lanes overlap inside one bracket, that is the wash he hears, and the flat cuts show where he changed pedal.
- The scrolling chord tags give him a written record of the progression he just improvised.
schemes.tiktok_value:
- Stops the scroll: glowing rainbow bars on near-black are the highest-contrast image there is. It reads first as a sound equaliser, then turns out to be music theory.
- The prism fold, 88 keys into 12 colours, is a shot people have not seen.
- Chord tags scrolling up work as subtitles for muted viewers.
- Because octaves merge and pedalled notes are hollow, fast pedalled runs (the most impressive moments) are also the most legible, where the current look turns to a wall.
- The tags invite screenshots and comments ('what is that Ab doing there?').
- Everything vital sits centre-left, clear of the action rail and caption area.
- With the loop seam, the last frame matches the first, so autoplay loops cleanly and repeat views add up.
schemes.sustain_behaviour:
- The per-lane history stores held energy and sustain energy in separate channels. Each is the max over all sounding notes of that pitch class, capped at 1.0. Eight octaves of C, or 200 pedalled notes, cannot make a lane brighter than one held note.
- Pedalled notes draw hollow: edge strokes plus at most an 18% fill, decaying with tau 1.1 s to a 0.12 floor while the pedal stays down. A long pedalled passage becomes outlined columns with dark centres, not a sheet. The blur stays readable, but dim.
- The field is one draw with no additive stacking.
- Peak linear brightness is about 1.4, so bloom (threshold 0.9) touches only the cores of held bars.
- The pedal itself is drawn once (the gutter bracket plus one hairline), not once per note.
schemes.build_sketch:
SHARED SCAFFOLDING (both presets, about 120 lines):
- A SCHEMES registry of objects {id, enter(), exit(), update(info, t, dt), restEnergy(), layout}, with a #scheme-select persisted in 'arsenal.piano.scheme'.
- 'trails' stays as the current look, untouched. Do not delete it.
- enter/exit toggles trailMesh.visible and scales the spark count; LAYOUT is keyed by scheme and framing.
- renderFrame calls scheme.update after overlay.update.
- Add schemeScene with an OrthographicCamera(0, w, h, 0) and a RenderPass(schemeScene, orthoCam) with clear=false and clearDepth=true, inserted as composer.insertPass(pass, 1). Scheme geometry then blooms while the Canvas2D overlay stays crisp after bloom.
- hook.fire(): spikes bloom.strength and a multiplier on cam.span; both damped.
- Loop seam: startRecording forces 0.4 s of rest state before the first captured note. stopRecording holds recorder.stop() until scheme.restEnergy() < 0.02 and overlay.labelAlpha < 0.02 (at most 2.5 s). The first and last frames then match.
- Raise the 9:16 lens shift (setViewOffset) so camera.project of the key-front corners lands at y <= 1520. Assert this in the CDP receipt.
- Engine: noteOff stores st.tRel = t, so sustain tails know their age.
- Everything advances per second, not per frame, so native-refresh rendering and 60 fps REC look the same.

PRISM-SPECIFIC (about 330 lines):
(1) History: DataTexture 13x512, RGBA, UnsignedByte, NearestFilter.
  - Columns 0-11: pitch class in fifths order. Channels R = held, G = sustain, B = onset flash.
  - Column 12: R = pedal down, G = chord-change flag.
  - A ring head advances at 140 rows/s through a time accumulator.
  - Each frame, compute heldE / susE / onset for 12 pitch classes by max over `sounding` and write the elapsed rows.
  - tex.needsUpdate, about 26 KB per frame.
(2) Field: a PlaneGeometry(820, 640) in schemeScene.
  - ShaderMaterial with glslVersion GLSL3; texelFetch two rows and mix them for sub-row smooth scrolling.
  - Uniforms: uHead, uRot (eased float; lane = mod(fi - uRot + 4, 12)), uLaneColor[12] from noteColor(pc, 100), uAlpha.
  - The same shader draws the lane guides, footers, hollow sustain, pedal bracket and hairlines.
  - About 130 lines of GLSL.
(3) Rays: InstancedBufferGeometry ribbon with 24 segments, RAY_MAX 64.
  - Each frame, write aX0 from new Vector3(keyX(m), RAIL_Y, TRAIL_Z).project(camera) converted to px.
  - Also aX1 (lane centre), aE and aColor. Sounding notes are at most 64, so the CPU cost is trivial.
  - About 90 lines.
(4) Chord tags: a pool of 8 CanvasTexture sprites (220x60) in overlayScene, each drawn once per chord change with the existing nameRuns / suffixRuns. About 60 lines.
(5) Rotation: take the relative major's fifths index from keyGuess, gated on silence, r and two agreeing estimates. About 30 lines.

Total about 450 lines including the shared part.

RISKS:
- The follow camera slides the keys under fixed lanes. The rays absorb this, but check they don't sweep visibly; if they do, capture aX0 at note-on and ease it.
- Wrap-fade during a rotation.
- A seam where the ring index wraps (keep rows as integers and use mod).
- The key guess wobbles in ambiguous passages (handled by the gates in (5)).
- A player who wants chromatic lane order: offer it as a toggle, but the hues will then be scrambled.

schemes.name: Fifths Clock
schemes.pitch: The keyboard fires comets into a glowing circle of fifths where every chord becomes a shape. Major and minor are mirror-image triangles, every dominant 7th cuts a line straight through the centre, and a ii-V-I is the shape stepping one notch round the clock.
schemes.visuals:
LAYOUT 1080x1920:
- y 0-230: empty.
- Chord label: reuse drawLabel at cy 340, size 140, with the note-name row around y 450.
- Ring: centre (540, 840), nodes on radius 320, outer stroke at r 350. It covers y 490-1190 and x 190-890, clear of the action rail.
- Comet band: y 1190-1330.
- Keyboard: key fronts at or above y 1520 (shared lens shift).
- Below y 1536: reflection only.

RING: the classic orientation, C at 12 o'clock, then clockwise G D A E B F#/Gb Db Ab Eb Bb F. Node letters sit in an overlay layer at r 385 (34px): 55% alpha at rest, 100% in the note colour while sounding. Spell them with spellAlone(pc, keyGuess.bias).

REST / THUMBNAIL: ring stroke in INK at 18%. The 12 node dots are 12px, in their own hue at 30%, so the rest frame is already a colour wheel. If a key has been guessed, its 7-node wedge shows at 6%. No idle motion.

NOTE-ON:
- A comet launches from the key's projected rail point and flies to its pitch-class node in 280 ms, ease-out-cubic.
- The path is a quadratic Bezier. The control point sits 260px above the start, offset sideways toward the node's side, so the comet arcs round the ring rather than through the label.
- The head is 10 + 8*vel px, with 6 tail samples 18 ms apart, fading.
- On arrival the node grows from 12px to 22 + 10*vel px, with an impulse of 1.3 that settles to held level over 150 ms.
- The key glows as it does today. Trails are off; sparks at 30%.

HELD:
- Filled node dots.
- A polygon joins all sounding pitch classes in circular order: 5px edges in the OKLab-averaged colour, interior fill at 10%.
- Two notes make a single line.
- Any pair 6 notches apart (a tritone) also gets a 3px white-cored diameter, drawn under a dark centre disc (r 120), so dominant chords visibly cut the clock in half.

NOTE-OFF (pedal up): the node shrinks to rest over 160 ms, and the polygon eases to a shape without it.

SUSTAIN (CC64):
- While the pedal is down, the outer stroke becomes 4px gold at 35% ('the ring is holding the sound').
- A note that is released but still pedalled becomes a hollow 3px ring, fading with tau 1.2 s to a 0.25 floor.
- Edges that touch a sustained-only vertex turn dashed (18px period) at 50%.
- On pedal-up, hollow nodes collapse in 160 ms, the polygon snaps to held notes only, and the gold fades over 250 ms. It reads as a clean clear.

CHORD CHANGE (when overlay.pop fires):
- One ring pulse: a circle from r 350 to 400 over 420 ms, alpha 0.35 to 0, in the root's colour.
- The old polygon becomes ghost 1 and all ghosts step inward. Ghost k draws edges only, at scale 0.86^k about the centre and alpha 0.35 * 0.6^k; keep 5. Past harmony recedes like a tunnel: Daniel's 'column' of time, folded into a circle.
- Each new vertex springs from the nearest old vertex angle (220 ms), so a ii-V-I shows as one shape stepping a notch counter-clockwise.

CENTRE: the chord's Roman numeral in the guessed key ('V7', 'bVII', 'iv'), 96px INK, with 'in C major' at 26px and 55% below it. Numerals outside the key are tinted with the root's hue.

KEY WEDGE: a sector over the 7 notes of the key at 7% alpha. When the key changes it rotates, eased with tau 0.6 s, only after two agreeing estimates.

OPTIONAL 'GUESS IT' toggle (in the HUD select, not a key: H and F are taken and G plays a note): for chords held at least 1.2 s, the label shows '?' for 1.0 s, then pops the name. Made for slow 'name this chord' clips.

16:9: ring centre (1440, 540), r 380; label on the left.
schemes.theory_value:
This makes the circle of fifths something he plays rather than a chart.
- Chord type is a shape, the same in every key. Major and minor triads are mirror-image triangles. sus2 and sus4 are three neighbouring notches, which is why they sound open. maj7 packs into 5 notches. dim7 is a perfect square, augmented an equilateral triangle, the whole-tone scale a hexagon.
- Dominant function becomes visible: the tritone diameter is the tension line, and it shows why V7 pulls toward I.
- Root motion is rotation. One notch counter-clockwise is a falling fifth (resolution); ii-V-I is two such steps. Big jumps are chromatic mediants.
- The key wedge makes borrowed chords (iv, bVI, bVII in a major key) light up outside the sector. Those are exactly the 'sad-happy' moves Daniel makes by instinct without knowing their names.
- Roman numerals teach function over letter names.
- The ghost tunnel shows the path a progression takes.
- Hollow pedalled nodes show which old notes are still ringing into the new chord.
schemes.tiktok_value:
- The circle of fifths is an instantly recognisable theory icon, so even the rest frame stops music-theory scrollers.
- The composition is symmetric and centred, ideal for 9:16, and survives 4:5 and 1:1 crops for Reels and Shorts reposts.
- Shapes morphing into shapes are 'oddly satisfying' viewing.
- A progression that returns to I returns to the identical shape, so a clip loops with a matching frame, helped by the shared loop seam.
- Numerals and shape facts invite comment corrections ('that's a borrowed iv'), and corrections are engagement.
- The 'guess it' reveal holds viewers until the name appears.
- Nothing builds up, so minute three looks as clean as second three, and long takes stay postable.
schemes.sustain_behaviour:
- Nothing builds up by design. The geometry budget is fixed: at most 12 nodes, one polygon and 5 ghosts, however long the pedal is held.
- Octaves merge per pitch class with max energy.
- Pedalled notes are hollow strokes decaying to a 25% floor, and their edges are dashed at 50%. A long pedalled wash reads as a faint dashed outline around the bright held shape.
- Polygon fill alpha is fixed at 10%, not added per note.
- The pedal state is drawn once (the gold outer stroke) instead of once per note.
- Pedal-up gives a crisp, visible clear that matches what the ear hears, so dense pedalling actually produces a readable rhythm of 'bloom, hold, clear'.
schemes.build_sketch:
Uses the shared scaffolding from Prism: scheme registry, schemeScene RenderPass before bloom, hook.fire, loop seam, lens shift, st.tRel.

(1) Clock face: one PlaneGeometry(800, 800) in schemeScene with a ShaderMaterial.
  - Uniforms: uNode[12] vec4 (linear rgb, held energy); uSus[12]; uVertAng[12], uVertSus[12] and uVertCount for the polygon; uWedge vec2 (angle, alpha); uPedal; uPulse (age, colour); uFill vec3; uScale, uAlpha and uEdgesOnly for ghosts.
  - The fragment shader draws: ring SDF, dots and hollows, a segment-SDF loop of at most 12, a convex fill from half-plane tests, tritone diameters, and dashes from the position along each edge.
  - About 140 lines of GLSL.
  - Ghosts: 5 material.clone() meshes with their own uniforms, 6 draws in total.
(2) Comets: InstancedBufferGeometry quads.
  - COMET_MAX 96, each with a head plus 6 lag samples: 672 instances.
  - Attributes: aP0 (px; set at note-on from new Vector3(keyX(m), RAIL_Y, TRAIL_Z).project(camera)), aP1 (node px), aCtrl, aT0, aDur, aLag, aColor, aVel.
  - The vertex shader evaluates the Bezier from uNow: zero per-frame CPU, like the current trails. Reuse the trails.start slot-recycling pattern.
  - About 80 lines.
(3) State:
  - Each frame, per-pc held and sustain energy by max over `sounding`; vertices are the sounding pcs sorted by fifths angle.
  - Morph: on a chord change, assign each new vertex to the nearest old angle (greedy is enough for 12 or fewer). Spring each angle with damp tau 0.07 along the shortest arc.
  - Fill colour: convert noteLch to OKLab a/b, average, damp tau 0.18, then convert to linear with the matrices already in oklchToLinear.
  - Ghosts: a ring buffer of 5 {angles, colour} snapshots with an eased index.
  - About 120 lines.
(4) THEORY addition (pure, and extend the node tests): numeral(info, key) -> {text, diatonic}.
  - degree = mod(pcOf(root) - tonic, 12), mapped to I, bII, II and so on.
  - Lower case when the template has a minor third.
  - Symbols: dim gives °, m7b5 gives ø7; 7, maj7 and 9 are kept.
  - Test cases in C major: G7 -> V7, Bb -> bVII, Fm -> iv, Bm7b5 -> viiø7. In A minor: E7 -> V7.
  - Show nothing for 'cluster'; for slash chords, the numeral plus a small '/bass'.
  - About 60 lines plus tests.
(5) Overlay:
  - Node-letter layer: one CanvasTexture, 1000x1000, redrawn only when the spelling bias or the sounding set changes.
  - Centre numeral layer, 300x200.
  - About 70 lines.
(6) trailMesh hidden, sparks at 0.3x.

Total about 500 lines.

RISKS:
- Comets crossing the label: the sideways control point handles it; verify with the demo's top-voice notes.
- The wedge wobbling on an unsure key guess: require two agreeing estimates and r >= 0.6.
- Bloom threshold 0.9 means node cores need about 1.0+ linear to glow: tune the energy scale, not bloom.
- The Roman numeral needs a reliable key. With no keyGuess, hide the numeral rather than guess.

log_to_banter:
Moments of the session: one log feeds both the banter and the TikTok pipeline.

1. Log. The page writes every MIDI event and every settled chord as JSONL:
   - {t, e:'on', m, v}, {t, e:'off', m}, {t, e:'ped', v}, {t, e:'rec', v}
   - and a chord line whenever overlay.shown changes: {t, e:'chord', name, notes, key, numeral, dur, pedal}
   It POSTs batches every 2 s to a sibling of /api/recordings, one file per session under state/arsenal/piano-log/.

2. Score. When he stops playing, an agent re-runs the node-tested THEORY block over the log and scores each chord move for interest:
   - the root falls outside the key wedge (borrowed or chromatic)
   - the root jumps 3 or more notches on the fifths circle
   - a tritone is present
   - the chord is held at least 1 s
   - the same move recurs across the session, which marks a habit

3. Post. The agent posts the top 3 as moments. Each moment has:
   - a timestamp
   - a plain-English name for the move, e.g. 'Ab major right after C: a borrowed bVI from C minor, the "epic sad" move'
   - one sentence on why it sounds the way it does
   - one question back, e.g. 'you land on this every time before you open up the voicing: is that the lift you're chasing?'

Moments whose timestamps fall inside a REC window double as clip candidates, each with a ready caption hook ('this one chord is why it sounds sad-happy'). Habits roll up across sessions into a 'harmonic fingerprint' the agents can tease him about and teach from.

angle: Music theory made visible. Everything drawn on screen is a fact the THEORY block already computes or can cheaply derive: each note's role in the chord, the chord's scale degree, root motion, how each voice moves, and tension. Daniel sees what his hands did and why it sounded that way. Scheme A keeps his idea of notes rising in columns and labels the theory onto them. Scheme B moves the harmony onto the circle of fifths. The app's colour already walks that circle (hue = 200 + 30*fifthsIndex), so the ring doubles as the colour legend, and a pitch-class ring can never draw more than 12 lit nodes, however much the pedal holds. That directly fixes the cyan-white wall seen in receipt r5-916-demo-b, where the columns wash over both the Dm9 label and the staff.

schemes.name: Voice Columns
schemes.pitch: Every rising column is coloured by its note's job in the chord (root, third, seventh, ninth). When the harmony changes, a thread arcs from each voice to where it went, so you can actually watch your 7th fall to the 3rd.
schemes.visuals: 9:16 at 1080x1920 (y measured from the top). 0-230 px stays empty. LABEL layer at cy 360, h 420 (150-570), three lines. (1) The chord name at 150 px, centred. (2) Role chips in voicing order from the bass up, e.g. 'R  b3  5  b7  9'. Each chip is 40 px Archivo 700 in its role colour with a 2 px underline, and these chips are the only legend. (3) A progression strip showing the last 4 Roman numerals, e.g. 'IVmaj9 -> V9 -> iii7 -> vi9', 44 px. The newest sits on the right at 100% ink, older ones at 60/38/20%. The strip slides left over 260 ms on a change. A dim 28 px caps key tag ('C MAJOR') follows it, shown only when the key guess is confident. Below the strip is a caption slot (30 px caps, 55% ink, 1.2 s) for at most one voice-leading callout per change. The STAFF stays at cy 800: noteheads take their role colour, with a 26 px role tag ('b7', '9') to the right of each notehead column. The trail field and keyboard stay where they are now. ROLE PALETTE (OKLCH): R 0.84/0.13/78 gold. Major 3 0.76/0.16/20 coral; minor b3 0.72/0.17/340 magenta, so major vs minor quality shows at a glance. Perfect 5 0.64/0.05/240 slate, which recedes on purpose. b5 and #5 0.70/0.14/250. b7 (and the dim7's bb7) 0.70/0.15/295 violet. maj7 0.78/0.12/200 ice cyan. Natural 9/11/13 and 2/4/6 0.78/0.14/160 mint. Altered b9/#9/#11/b13 0.74/0.18/48 hot orange, the tension colour. Passing or unassigned 0.90/0.02/250, drawn at 0.35 width. CLEAR ZONES: the trail fragment shader dims colour to x0.18 inside two soft rectangles (label 150,170-930,590; staff 160,590-920,1040; 70 px feather). Columns read as passing behind frosted glass, and the text and staff stay legible. NOTE-ON: the column starts in the role colour computed against the live detection, which already includes the new note. The key's emissive glow and the spark burst use the same colour. If the settled chord disagrees within 150 ms, the whole instance is recoloured, not split. NOTE-OFF: the bright held bar ends at the release point and a thin filament continues below it while the note still sounds. SUSTAIN PEDAL: while down, the gold rail line brightens from x0.9 to x1.8 (80 ms ease). On pedal-up, a 0.03-unit warm-white hairline (alpha 0.28) is drawn across the span of the notes it cut, and it rises with the trails. The gap between that hairline and the chord-change thread shows pedal timing. CHORD CHANGE (fires when the overlay settles a new chord name): (1) Held notes older than 150 ms whose role changed are split. The old instance ends at t with a square top and a new instance starts at t with a square bottom in the new colour, so a held C visibly turns from gold (root of C) to slate (5th of F). (2) Voice threads appear at rung height y = RAIL_Y + (now - tChange)*6.5, so they rise glued to the columns. Each arcs from the old voice's key x to the new voice's key x. Width is 0.07 (bass 0.11). Arch height is 0.25 + 0.06*|semitones moved|. Colour grades from the old role to the new role along the arc. Steps of 1-2 semitones draw at full brightness, leaps of 3-7 at 30%, and anything larger is not drawn. A common tone gets a 0.22 diamond glint on its column. (3) The strip slides and the label pops as it does now. (4) The caption shows the highest-priority match, in this order: '7TH -> 3RD', 'LEADING TONE -> ROOT', 'CONTRARY MOTION', 'N COMMON TONES'. 16:9: the label goes top-left with the strip under it and the staff stays on the right, so both clear zones move with LAYOUT.
schemes.theory_value: Roles explain voicings: which note is the colour note, which is doubled, and whether the 5th is doing anything (usually not, which is why it can be dropped). Coral vs magenta makes chord quality visible before the name is read. The threads are voice leading: smooth progressions draw short bright arcs, and V7->I shows the textbook resolutions as a violet-to-coral arc (7th down to 3rd) and a coral-to-gold arc (leading tone up to root). A held note that changes colour shows one pitch taking a new meaning under new harmony, which is how pivot tones and pedal points work. The Roman strip teaches function as a pattern you can move to any key. The built-in demo reads IVmaj9 V9 iii7 vi9 ii9 V13 Imaj9 Imaj7/3, the 'royal road' progression running into a ii-V-I, and that becomes visible. Pedal-up hairlines teach legato pedalling: lift just after the change, not before it.
schemes.tiktok_value: It keeps the rising-column look Daniel already loves and adds 'wait, what?' moments that reward a rewatch: a held note changing colour mid-column, or two voices braiding past each other. The progression strip is a caption people screenshot ('ii9 -> V13 -> Imaj9'), and arguing over numerals drives comments. The frosted clear zones mean the chord name survives the recording even in the densest pedalled section.
schemes.sustain_behaviour: Only the held part of a column is a full-width bar with a halo. Below the release point, under the pedal, the column narrows to a filament: the SDF half-width is mix(0.3*vW, vW, held) per fragment, which also gives a tapered needle at the release point. The halo term is multiplied by held, so the filament has no halo, and filament energy is 0.18*exp(-age/0.7). A new uniform uTailGain = clamp(5/sounding.size, 0.35, 1), eased with tau 0.3 s, scales only the filaments; held bars never dim. Filaments are about 0.19 units wide on a 1.0 key pitch, so neighbouring keys don't overlap and additive stacking cannot reach white. Pedal-carried notes that are not in the settled chord render in the near-white passing colour at 50%, so harmonic blur reads as grey mist rather than a rainbow. Clear zones keep label and staff legible no matter what. Every pedal lift leaves a hairline edge, so long pedalled passages still show their structure.
schemes.build_sketch: Reuses keys, the instanced trail mesh and its clock-driven vertex shader, sparks, bloom, the overlay layers, Theory.detect with its spellings (role labels come out correct for free, because letters are already spelled from the root), estimateKey, and noteColor/noteCss. New code: (a) THEORY, pure and node-tested. roleOf(info) maps each midi to {label, family}: steps = mod(n.letter - root.letter, 7) and semis = mod(midi - pcOf(root), 12) give 0->R; 1->b9/9/#9 (or 2 in sus2); 2->b3/3; 3->11/#11 (or 4 in sus4); 4->b5/5/#5; 5->b13/13 (6 in 6-chords, bb7 in dim7); 6->b7/7. romanOf(info, key): degree = mod(root.letter - tonic.letter, 7); the prefix b or # comes from the difference to the scale pitch (minor keys accept a raised 6th or 7th). Lowercase if the third is minor; dim adds a degree sign, m7b5 is 'o7' (half-diminished), aug adds '+'. Inversions render as '/3', '/5', '/7'. voiceMatch(prevMidis, nextMidis): bass to bass and top to top, inner voices by brute force when there are 6 or fewer (else greedy), minimising sum of |delta|, returning pairs. captionOf(pairs, prevRoles, nextRoles). Pins: the demo's numerals, and G7->C producing 'B->C leading tone' and 'F->E 7th->3rd'. (b) Outside THEORY: key hysteresis. The displayed key changes only after a new estimate has led for 3 s with r >= 0.6; below that, numerals fall back to chord symbols. (c) A ROLE_LCH table and a 'role' COLOUR.mode. (d) Trails: an aCaps attribute (bit 0 square bottom, bit 1 square top; the corner radius goes to 0 on that side), per-fragment tail width, halo multiplied by held, uTailGain, and uniforms uClearA/uClearB (canvas px converted to GL y = H - y), plus trails.split(ref, t, colour) and trails.recolor(ref, colour). (e) Threads: a second InstancedBufferGeometry on PlaneGeometry(1,1,20,1) with aX0, aX1, aT, aArch, aW, aC0, aC1, aAlpha. It is a 160-slot ring buffer, and the vertex shader bends s into x = mix(x0,x1,s), y = rung + arch*sin(pi*s). Additive, with the same top fade as the trails. (f) A chord-commit hook: overlay.update calls onChordCommit(prev, next, t) where it replaces this.shown (the pop assignment). Each chord keeps 'voices', meaning the notes attacked or held while it was pending or shown. (g) drawLabel gains chips, strip and caption; drawStaff gains role tags. (h) A scheme select stored at arsenal.piano.scheme ('trails' | 'voices' | 'compass'). Roughly 380 lines. Everything is driven by clock() and damp(dt), so 60 Hz or the monitor's native rate look identical. Risks: key-guess flips (hysteresis plus numeral fallback); split churn on rolled chords (150 ms recolour window, split only on a settled change); detection folding pedal carry-over into the chord (use the settled label and the passing colour for non-members); thread clutter in busy two-hand passages (at most 10 per change, none for changes under 250 ms apart).

schemes.name: Fifths Compass
schemes.pitch: Your chords become shapes on the circle of fifths: major and minor are mirror-image triangles, every tritone is a glowing laser straight across the circle, and when the tension resolves the whole ring exhales in a shockwave.
schemes.visuals: 9:16 at 1080x1920 (y measured from the top). 0-230 px stays empty. LABEL at cy 330, h 300: the chord name at 130 px, with the note-name line in pitch colours as today. The staff is hidden in this preset because the ring is the notation. RING: centre (540, 820), R = 320 px, so nodes span x 220-860 and stay left of TikTok's right-hand button rail (x > 940). Node k sits at phi = 30deg*fifthsIndex(pc), clockwise from the top: x = cx + R*sin(phi), y = cy - R*cos(phi). So C is at the top, G one step clockwise, F one step anticlockwise. Node colours are exactly the existing pitch OKLCH, which makes the ring the legend for the trails and keys. An idle node is a 2 px outline, radius 30, at L 0.40 C 0.05. Letter names sit outside at r 385 (40 px Archivo 700, 45% ink, 90% when lit), spelled with Theory.spellAlone(pc, key.bias), and are redrawn only when the key bias changes. KEY WEDGE: an annular sector at r 280-360 covering the 7 diatonic positions (tonic position k-1 through k+5), filled oklch(0.30 0.05 tonicHue) at alpha 0.45 with a 20 px angular feather. The tonic gets an 8 px gold dot at r 250. The wedge is hidden when key confidence is below 0.6. On a key change it rotates the shorter way with tau 0.6 s, so a modulation is seen as the wedge turning. CHORD POLYGON: all 12 vertices always exist. A lit vertex sits on its node; an unlit vertex sits on the hull edge between its lit neighbours, interpolated by angle. Vertices ease with tau 0.1 s, so shapes morph without pops. Fill alpha is 0.14 + 0.10*T in the mean of the lit colours, and edges are 3 px ribbons graded between their endpoint colours. TRITONE LASERS: every sounding pitch-class pair 6 apart (always diametrically opposite on the ring) draws a 6 px diameter ribbon, core oklch(0.80 0.19 35) with an 18 px halo, brightness 0.6 + 0.4*T. ROOT ARCS: on a chord change, an arc runs inside the ring at r 230 from the old root to the new root the shorter way, with a 14 px arrowhead. Colour by root motion: one step anticlockwise (down a fifth) is gold h78; one step clockwise is blue h230; 2 steps mint; 3-4 steps violet; 6 steps (a tritone) red-orange. The last 4 arcs persist at alpha 1/0.5/0.25/0.12, so ii-V-I draws as two gold steps D->G->C. CENTRE TEXT (overlay, drawn after bloom so it stays crisp): the Roman numeral at 120 px, 88% ink ('V9'); 'in C' at 30 px and 50% below it; a cadence caption in 30 px caps at 60% for 1.5 s under that. TENSION: a 120-degree gauge arc under the ring at r 400, from 210 to 330 degrees. It has a 6 px track at 12% ink, and its fill runs 0..T with colour easing from oklch(0.70 0.08 230) to oklch(0.78 0.16 40). A centre radial glow (r 0-300) takes the same hue at alpha 0.06 + 0.16*T. All eased with tau 0.35 s, with no noise. KEYBOARD: stays at the bottom. Trails are kept but uTop is lowered so columns fade out by screen y ~1200, a short flame bed under the ring. NOTE-ON: a comet leaves the key's rail point (projected through the camera to canvas px) and flies into its node along a quadratic Bezier with control point (keyScreenX, 1180), over 0.32 s ease-in. The head is 10-16 px depending on velocity, followed by 5 trailing dots. On impact the node radius goes 30->44 and flashes +10 px, decaying over 0.25 s. The polygon vertex extends. NOTE-OFF: with the pedal up, the node fades to idle over 0.25 s and its vertex collapses onto the hull. With the pedal down, the node becomes a hollow 5 px ring. SUSTAIN PEDAL: when pressed, the SMuFL 'Ped.' glyph (U+E650) appears at (150, 1180), 36 px, 40% ink. When lifted, all hollow rings shrink and fade together over 0.18 s, a visible clearing, and the glyph fades. CHORD CHANGE: the polygon morphs, the root arc draws, lasers appear or dissolve, the numeral cross-fades over 0.15 s, and tension eases. A resolution fires when T drops by at least 0.2 and the root fell a fifth, landed on the tonic, or a tritone vanished. It sends a shockwave ring from the new root node (radius 44->300 px over 0.7 s, 4 px wide, alpha (1-k)^2, root colour), and any vanished laser dissolves with a 0.2 s white flash. 16:9: the ring goes on the right third (cx 1480, cy 440, R 250) with the label left as now.
schemes.theory_value: Circle-of-fifths geometry turns abstract facts into space. A key is a contiguous 7-node wedge, so out-of-key notes are literally outside the lit region, and a modulation is a rotation. Chord qualities are fixed shapes in any key: major and minor triads are mirror-image triangles, an augmented triad is an equilateral triangle, a dominant 7th is the shape that contains a diameter (its tritone), and a diminished 7th is a square made of two lasers. That shows why dim7 chords are symmetrical and ambiguous. Root arcs show harmonic gravity: strong progressions walk anticlockwise one step at a time, and mediant jumps look like jumps. The gauge, lasers and shockwave tie the felt tension and release to what's on screen. Cadence captions name what just happened: authentic (V->I), plagal (IV->I), deceptive (V->vi), backdoor (bVII7 or iv -> I), tritone sub (bII7->I), secondary dominant (dom7 falling a fifth onto a diatonic chord other than I, captioned 'V7/ii' and so on). Comets from widely spread keys converging on one node teach octave equivalence: a spread voicing is still the same few pitch classes.
schemes.tiktok_value: It's clean, symmetric geometry that looks unlike every falling-notes piano video, and it reads in a thumbnail. The tritone laser snapping into a shockwave lands exactly on the audible release, a built-in payoff beat that makes loops satisfying. Captions like 'DECEPTIVE CADENCE' are hooks on their own, and the shapes invite 'what shape is a sus chord?' comments. Because the picture is bounded to 12 nodes, it stays clean in the heavily pedalled playing that washed out the current scheme.
schemes.sustain_behaviour: Grouping by pitch class caps the picture: however many notes the pedal holds, at most 12 nodes and 6 lasers are ever drawn, so it cannot wash out. A held pitch class is a filled node. A pitch class sounding only through the pedal is a hollow ring whose energy decays from 0.55 to 0.25 over 2 s, still sounding but visibly secondary. Pedal-only vertices sit at 85% radius with their edges at 35% alpha, so the polygon shows the chord your hands hold, surrounded by the pedal's halo. Tension counts pedal-only pitch classes at weight 0.5 (a pair counts at its lower weight), so pedal blur honestly raises the gauge. A pedal lift collapses every hollow ring at once, a visible clearing gesture. Under the ring, the keyboard trails are short (faded by y ~1200) and use the same narrow, halo-free tail filament as Voice Columns, so the flame bed never reaches the ring or the label.
schemes.build_sketch: Reuses noteColor/noteCss (nodes match trails and keys exactly), Theory.detect, estimateKey and spellAlone, the keys, the trails (only uTop and the tail change), sparks for comet impacts, the overlay canvas layers (label, plus a new centre layer for numeral and caption and a letters layer), UnrealBloom, and the romanOf, key hysteresis and onChordCommit hook shared with Voice Columns. New code: (a) ringScene plus OrthographicCamera(0,W,H,0), drawn through a second RenderPass(ringScene, ringCam) with clear=false and clearDepth, inserted after the main RenderPass and before bloom. Nodes and lasers glow; the text overlay stays crisp. (b) Nodes: one 12-instance quad mesh with an SDF disc/ring shader (aFill, aHollow, aColor, aFlash). (c) Wedge, centre glow and gauge: one quad covering the ring with a polar fragment shader (uKeyAngle, uKeyShow, uTension, uTensionColor). (d) Polygon: a dynamic 12-triangle fan BufferGeometry and 12 edge ribbons, with vertex positions computed on the CPU each frame (12 points, negligible). (e) Lasers: 6 instanced ribbons. Arcs: 4 instanced 24-segment ribbons bent in the vertex shader from angle attributes. Shockwaves: 2 instanced ring quads. (f) Comets: 64x6 instanced points with aP0, aP1, aBirth, positioned by uNow in the shader. The start point comes from new Vector3(keyX(m), RAIL_Y, TRAIL_Z).project(camera) at spawn; comets merge per pitch class within 80 ms for rolls and glissandos. (g) THEORY, pure and node-tested. fifthsPos(pc). tensionOf(weightedPcs, info, key) = clamp(0.32*min(2,tritonePairs)/2 + 0.20*min(3,semitonePairs)/3 + 0.22*outOfKeyFraction + 0.18*dom + 0.05*sus + 0.03*slash, 0, 1). A root-to-maj7 pair counts half. dom = 1 for dominant-family suffixes whose root isn't the tonic, 0.7 for dim, dim7 and m7b5. Pins: C in C = 0, G7 in C ~0.34, G7b9 ~0.61, Cdim7 ~0.56, Dm9 ~0.07. cadenceOf(prevInfo, nextInfo, key) returns the caption strings above. Roughly 480 lines. Every animation reads clock() or damp(dt), so it is refresh-rate independent at 60 Hz or native, and REC stays paced at 60. Risks: the tension weights are a heuristic, so keep them in one table and tune by ear against the pins. A wrong key guess breaks the wedge and numerals (confidence gate, fallback to chord symbols). Angle and y-axis sign mistakes between the ortho camera and canvas px (test with C at the top and G clockwise). Extra render-pass cost at 1080x1920 is small.

log_to_banter: A mark-and-explain notebook. (1) Logging: the page appends every MIDI event (note-on/off with velocity; the raw CC64 value 0-127, not just down/up, so half-pedalling shows) to a new POST /api/notelog. It also writes one line per settled chord: {t, name, roman, key, keyConfidence, roles, tension, cadence, voiceMoves, pedalBlur}. Lines go to state/arsenal/notelogs/<date>/<session>.jsonl in the same append-only style as TakeLedger's events.jsonl, with REC start and stop times so log time maps onto the video. (2) Marking: one KeyLab pad, MIDI-learned once and saved to localStorage (or the M key), drops a {type:'mark'} event meaning 'I don't understand what I just did', without leaving the keyboard. (3) Digest: a small Python script folds each session into a one-page brief. It lists common progressions as key-independent Roman-numeral sequences, favourite voicings as interval stacks from the bass (e.g. left hand 'R 5', right hand 'b3 b7 9'), and habits with counts (V->vi vs V->I, pedal lifts before vs after the chord change, the most-used colour tone). Each marked moment comes with the 8 seconds of harmony around it and its video timestamp. (4) Banter: agents start from the brief and open on one concrete moment. For example: 'At 3:12 you marked Bb/C going to Fmaj7. Bb/C over a C bass is really C9sus4: a dominant whose 3rd is swapped for a 4th, which is why it lands on F more softly than C7 would. You did this 6 times tonight. Want to try it once with the E added and hear the difference?' Daniel answers at the piano, and the next session's digest checks whether the move shows up, so the conversation rests on what he actually played rather than generic theory.

angle:
MilkDrop-style psychedelia, with every photon still coming from a sounding MIDI note at a place that means something: its key column (Scheme A) or its spoke on the circle of fifths (Scheme B). Feedback, colour physics and audio only move and age that light; they never invent it.

Why the pedalled passage turned into a wall: the trails use additive blending. Twenty pitch colours added together sum toward cyan-white, and UnrealBloomPass then blooms the sum. Both schemes swap additive light for a shared colour-physics core, an OKLab energy accumulator:
- The feedback buffer stores sum(Lab * e) in rgb and sum(e) in alpha.
- Display hue = the weighted mean hue.
- Lightness = 0.72 * (1 - exp(-0.9 * E)), a saturating curve that is capped below the bloom threshold.
- Chroma = the palette's 0.155 * clamp(|mean ab| / 0.12, 0, 1).

Result: a dense pedalled passage gets brighter only up to a ceiling and never goes white. A diatonic passage stays saturated in its arc of fifths-hues. A chromatic cluster across the whole wheel averages to a dim silver, which is honest: saturation now tracks tonal focus.

Frame rate: Daniel asked for 60 fps or monitor-native. The render loop already runs at native refresh (rAF), and REC is paced at 60. The one new rule is that both feedback sims advance on a fixed 60 Hz step (an accumulator, at most 4 steps per rendered frame). The picture then looks the same, and records the same, at 60, 144 or 240 Hz. A per-frame decay would change the look with the refresh rate.

CC64: already wired into the notes engine (the sounding map, the sustain flag, the dim trail tail). Both schemes read sounding and sustain and use one damper metaphor: pedal down makes the field viscous and persistent; pedal up is a drain of about 300 ms. If his pedal sends continuous CC64, the visuals can lerp with depth while notes still switch at 64.

House feedback laws from PLAY-NIGHT-SPEC, kept in both:
- two history render targets, ping-ponged, never read and written in the same pass
- hue applied only to freshly injected colour, never inside the loop
- history cleared on scheme switch and on applyFraming
- RGBA8 fallback: bias Lab by 0.5 and subtract a 1/255 floor
- no noise textures and no per-frame jitter; motion comes from deterministic sines on rates that never line up
- window.__piano.snapshot() clears history and settles 90 fixed steps, so a receipt is a true still

Both are new presets beside the current look, not replacements.

schemes.name: Resonance Plumes
schemes.pitch: Every key breathes a column of coloured smoke straight up the screen. Lift the pedal and the room exhales; hold it and the overtones you never played start ghosting up beside the notes you did. A crunchy voicing makes the air churn.
schemes.visuals:
LAYOUT (9:16): keyboard, chord label (cy 318) and staff (cy 800) all stay where they are now. The rail sits at about y 1365 px.

THE FIELD
- A world-space plane at z = TRAIL_Z - 0.02, x -28.5..28.5, y RAIL_Y..RAIL_Y+80. The follow camera and lens shift pan it for free, and uTop is already computed.
- Sim texture: 1024x1536 RGBA16F, about 18 texels per world unit.
- Each 60 Hz step does semi-Lagrangian advection straight up at TRAIL_SPEED (6.5 units/s), so plumes rise at the same speed the bars do now.
- Sideways flow = uTurb * 0.9 units/s * (sin(0.37y + 0.61t + 0.21x) + 0.6 sin(0.83y - 0.97t + 0.53x)), multiplied by smoothstep(1.5, 6.0, height above the rail). Columns stay pinned to their keys and only sway higher up. No noise, no jitter.
- Lightness fades out between 60% and 100% of uTop.

HOT CORES: the existing instanced trails stay, but only as thin cores: width x0.3 and sustain-tail gain 0 (two new uniforms, uWidthScale and uTailGain). Only held notes cross the bloom threshold; the smoke never blooms.

NOTE-ON: an emitter at keyX(m) injects OKLab colour (from noteLch) within 0.9 units above the rail.
- strength 3 * (0.5 + 0.5 * vel/127)
- gaussian width 0.55 x key width
- key dip, key glow, sparks (burst) and noteLights all stay

NOTE-OFF (no pedal): injection stops, the plume detaches from the rail and floats up as a free puff. keep = 0.992 per step (half-life 1.4 s), gone in about 4 s.

CHORD CHANGE (the moment overlay.shown changes name and the label pops): a harmonic ripple from the bass note's x.
- a sideways displacement wave running outward along the rail at 14 units/s
- 0.5 s life, only within 12 units above the rail
- strength 0.4 + 0.6 * |root motion in fifths| / 6, so a V-I nudges the smoke and a tritone move shoves it

LEGIBILITY: the display shader reads gl_FragCoord and dims smoke to 38% lightness inside soft ellipses, like smoke seen through glass:
- label: centre (540, 318), rx 520, ry 170
- staff: centre (540, 800), rx 430, ry 300
The top 12% and bottom 20% hold only fading smoke and the physical keys.

16:9: identical in world space; the masks come from the 16:9 LAYOUT.
schemes.theory_value:
1) ROUGHNESS YOU CAN SEE. uTurb comes from a pure Theory.roughness(notes) over real semitone distances, so voicing matters, not only the chord name.
- Pair weights: 1 -> 1.0, 2 -> 0.5, 6 -> 0.55, 11 -> 0.35, 13 -> 0.4, 3 or 4 -> 0.1, 5 or 7 -> 0.03.
- Distances beyond 24 count half; pairs below C3 count x1.5 (low-register mud).
- Pairs are weighted by sqrt(v_i * v_j); sustained notes count 0.5.
- Target = clamp(sum / sqrt(pairs), 0, 1), eased with a 0.4 s attack and 1.2 s release.
A Cmaj7 with the B a major 7th above C flows calm. Put the B a semitone under the C and the column churns. Move a low 3rd up an octave and the mud clears.

2) SYMPATHETIC RESONANCE. With the pedal down, a real piano's undamped strings ring at the played notes' overtones. Ghost wisps rise at partials 2-6 (+12, +19, +24, +28, +31 semitones) at strength 0.35/n, in the fundamental's colour. Where two notes share a partial, the wisps add: C and G both feed G5, so a fifth shows a bright shared column, while a minor 2nd shares nothing. That is the physical reason octaves and fifths blend.

3) SATURATION = TONAL FOCUS. Diatonic playing keeps a coherent arc of hues. Chromatic playing averages toward silver.
schemes.tiktok_value:
- Plumes read as ink in water, expensive rather than a MIDI roll.
- The pedal-lift exhale is a clean visual beat to cut on.
- The churn is a ready caption hook: 'watch what a minor 9th does to the air'.
- At rest the frame is black with a crisp label, so first frame and thumbnail stay legible.
- Columns rise exactly over their keys, so viewers can see which key made which plume.
schemes.sustain_behaviour:
HELD: a full-strength plume attached to the key, plus the thin hot core that blooms.

RELEASED UNDER THE PEDAL:
- the core ends, and the attachment thins to a tether (width 0.22 x key, strength 0.5 * exp(-age / 1.8 s))
- the tether sways like a vibrating string: 0.6 Hz at A0 up to 2.0 Hz at C8, amplitude 0.08 units
- the 8 most recent sounding notes add their partial-ghost wisps
Pedalled notes read as thin, living, dimming threads, clearly different from held columns.

PEDAL DOWN: keep rises from 0.992 to 0.996 (half-life 2.9 s) and the amber railLine brightens x1.6. With continuous CC64, both lerp with depth.

PEDAL UP (damper drop): keep falls to 0.93 for 300 ms, so the haze drains in one breath; tethers are cut and the rail dims.

ANTI-WASHOUT:
(a) OKLab energy accumulation caps lightness at 0.72 and never goes white
(b) a sustained emitter injects at most 1/6 of a held one
(c) all emitter strengths x 1/sqrt(max(1, n/4)), where n = sounding count
(d) glass-pane dimming behind the label and staff
(e) emitters capped at 64: held first, then sustained by recency, then partials
(f) the smoke sits below the bloom threshold; only held cores bloom
schemes.build_sketch:
REUSES: keyX, isBlack, RAIL_Y, TRAIL_Z, TRAIL_SPEED, trailUniforms.uTop, noteLch (add oklchToOklab: a = C cos h, b = C sin h), the sounding map and sustain flag, overlay.shown and pop for chord changes, burst / lightNote / updateKeys unchanged, the instanced trail shader (two new uniforms), the audioIn analyser.

NEW CODE (about 380 lines):
1) Pure Theory.roughness(notes, vels) and Theory.partials(midi) inside the THEORY block, with node tests.
2) A `plumes` module:
   - two WebGLRenderTarget(1024, 1536, {type: HalfFloatType, depthBuffer: false}), ping-ponged
   - a FullScreenQuad (three/addons/postprocessing/Pass.js) running the sim ShaderMaterial
   - uniforms: uPrev, uDt = 1/60, uKeep, uTurb, uT, uEm[EMITTERS] vec4 (x, strength, width, swayHz), uEmLab[EMITTERS] vec3, uEmCount, uShock vec4 (x, t0, strength, 0)
   - EMITTERS = 64, injected as a #define from one JS constant
   - the emitter loop early-outs for texels more than 0.9 units above the rail, so it runs on about 1% of texels
3) A scene Mesh(PlaneGeometry(57, 80)) with the display ShaderMaterial: OKLab to linear, chroma restore, glass masks from LAYOUT, height fade. depthWrite false, normal blending.
4) A fixed-step accumulator in renderFrame; the sim runs before composer.render.
5) Optional audio seasoning, zero with no input: getFloatFrequencyData on the existing analyser. Bass flux adds up to +0.15 to uTurb; level scales rise speed by up to 12% either way.
6) A scheme select entry. Switching and applyFraming clear both targets; snapshot() clears and runs 90 steps.

RISKS:
- One extra 1.5 M-texel pass per step on the host with an AMD TDR history. The fixed 60 Hz step bounds it, and it shares the same renderer (no second GPU context).
- The RGBA8 fallback cannot store negative Lab: bias it and add the subtraction floor.
- Bilinear advection diffuses: about 4 texels sigma (0.2 units) after 5 s, so columns stay distinct.
- The hot-core change touches the trail shader: gate the new uniforms by scheme so today's look stays byte-identical as its own preset.

schemes.name: Fifths Maelstrom
schemes.pitch: Your notes fly off the keys like comets into a slowly spinning circle-of-fifths whirlpool, with the chord name sitting in its black eye. The key you're in lights up as one arc, a borrowed chord flares on the dark side, and every ii-V-I winds the whole thing another turn.
schemes.visuals:
LAYOUT (9:16), a per-scheme LAYOUT entry:
- lens shift 0.25 -> 0.29, so the rail drops to about y 1440 and the keys sit lower
- staff moves up to cy 410, s 17 (about 280-570 px with a ledger line), clear of the top 12% (230 px)
- wheel centre C = (540, 1000) px, ring radius R = 320
- octave sets radius: r = R + 60 - 120 * (m-21)/87, so bass sits on the outer rim and treble inside (band 260-380 px)
- eye: ellipse rx 250, ry 180 at C with a 30 px soft edge, where feedback is multiplied to 0; the chord label moves into it (cy 1000, size 116, shrunk with measureRuns to fit 0.8 x 2rx)
- a Canvas2D ring layer (makeLayer, 900x900) draws the 12 letter names at R+95 in 30% ink plus a small tonic tick; redrawn only on key change

FIELD
- Screen space: two 540x960 RGBA16F targets, ping-ponged.
- Drawn as an additive full-screen quad in overlayScene under the label and staff (renderOrder -1, toneMapped false), so it never goes through bloom.
- Each 60 Hz step samples prev at the centre-relative UV rotated by spin * dt and scaled by zoom 0.988: light spirals inward and dies in the eye.
- keep = 0.975 inside R+100 and 0.90 beyond, so fog never reaches the staff.

ANGLE: theta(pc) = fifthsIndex(pc) * 30 deg - wheelRot, clockwise from 12 o'clock. This is the same walk the palette's hue already takes (hue = 200 + 30 * fifthsIndex), so position and colour always agree.

NOTE-ON: a comet launches from the key top projected to screen: new Vector3(keyX(m), RAIL_Y, TRAIL_Z).project(camera).
- It flies a quadratic Bezier (control point straight above the key at y 1150 px) to its ring point in 0.45 s, easing out.
- The head is a gaussian splat of radius 10 + 8 * vel/127 px, injected every step; the feedback smear draws the tail.
- So notes still go up a column from the keys; the column just bends into the wheel.
- Key dip, glow, sparks and noteLights stay; the instanced trails are hidden.

HELD, ON ARRIVAL: a star at the ring point, 14 px, strength 0.9 * vel/127, breathing +/-10% at 0.5 Hz.

NOTE-OFF: the star stops injecting; its light spirals inward and is gone in about 1 s.

CHORD CHANGE (overlay.shown changes name):
(1) Root-motion arc: a bright stroke injected along the ring from the old root's spoke to the new root's, the short way, over 0.25 s.
(2) Spin impulse: d = signed fifths steps of the root motion (-6..+6). spin += 0.12 rad/s per step, clockwise for sharpward moves, anticlockwise for flatward. Damping tau 3 s, clamp +/-0.6 rad/s. A tritone (6 steps) keeps the spin and fires the shock at full strength.
(3) Shock ring: a UV displacement expanding from the eye edge at 0.9 screen-heights/s with strength 0.004 * |d|. A tritone move jolts; a fifth barely ripples.

KEY: wheelRot eases the short way (tau 2.5 s) so the key's seven-note arc is centred at 12 o'clock. The arc centre is the relative major tonic + 2 fifths (for C major that is D, and C sits at 10 o'clock). The rotation switches only when estimateKey's r beats the current key's by 0.05 for 3 s; a null key holds the last rotation.

AUDIO (seasoning, only with an input selected): a bass beat punches zoom to 0.975, decaying over 0.18 s. The beat fires when bass power is over 1.6x its 1.5 s mean and rising, with a 180 ms refractory period, as play.js does. Level scales injection 0.85-1.15.

16:9: wheel at (1440, 540) with R 300, label in the eye, staff at (430, 300) s 18, keyboard full width.
schemes.theory_value:
THE KEY BECOMES GEOMETRY.
- A diatonic passage lights one contiguous 7-spoke arc centred at the top; by construction at least 5/12 of the wheel stays dark.
- Out-of-key notes land on the dark side. Left of the arc is the flat side: the borrowed iv, bVI and bVII from the parallel minor bring Ab, Eb and Bb in C. Right of the arc is the sharp side: F#, C# and G#, the leading tones of secondary dominants.
- Relative major and minor share one arc and differ only in the tonic tick. The arc's symmetric centre is the Dorian tonic, a free fact.

ROOT MOTION BECOMES MOTION.
- Descending-fifths progressions wind the wheel steadily one way. The demo's Dm9 -> G13 -> Cmaj9 is -1, -1: two anticlockwise notches.
- A plagal IV-I (F -> C) turns it one notch the other way.
- A tritone substitution fires the biggest shock the wheel has.

When Daniel does something by ear that feels spicy, he sees where it sits relative to home and how far the root jumped. The overlay label already names the chord; the wheel shows its function.
schemes.tiktok_value:
- A slowly spinning mandala with the chord name in a black eye survives any thumbnail and loops cleanly.
- Cadences give a wind-and-settle you can cut on.
- The dark-side flare is a ready caption: 'the chord that shouldn't work'.
- Comets leaving the keys keep it obvious that a human is playing.
- Eye, wheel and staff all sit inside the TikTok-safe band (230-1536 px).
schemes.sustain_behaviour:
HELD: a bright star at its spoke.

RELEASED UNDER THE PEDAL: the star dissolves into an arc segment +/-8 deg wide at its octave radius, strength 0.18 * exp(-age / 1.6 s). Pedalled notes read as haze on the wheel, never as stars.

PEDAL DOWN:
- keep rises from 0.975 to 0.988
- spin damping halves, so the wheel coasts like undamped strings
- a faint full 360 deg hairline appears at R (12% ink, in the ring layer): the dampers are up
- with continuous CC64, all three lerp with depth

PEDAL UP: the hairline snaps off, and keep drops to 0.90 for 250 ms so the haze drains into the eye.

ANTI-WASHOUT:
(a) the shared OKLab accumulator: lightness at most 0.70, never white; whole-wheel clusters go silver
(b) diatonic playing can light at most 7 of 12 spokes, by construction
(c) the eye kill protects the label; the fast outer decay protects the staff
(d) injection x 1/sqrt(max(1, n/4))
(e) the field bypasses bloom entirely
(f) the same pitch class in different octaves stacks at different radii instead of piling onto one point
schemes.build_sketch:
REUSES: fifthsIndex and noteLch (colour and angle are the same number), keyX plus camera.project for comet launch points, Theory.estimateKey / keyGuess (already recomputed on detectDirty), overlay.shown and pop, makeLayer / disposeLayer / measureRuns for the ring letters and label fitting, LAYOUT (add per-scheme entries), sounding and sustain, burst / lightNote / updateKeys unchanged, the audioIn analyser, and the OKLab accumulator plus fixed-step clock from Resonance Plumes if that is built first.

NEW CODE (about 500 lines):
1) Pure Theory additions with node tests: fifthsSteps(fromPc, toPc) -> -6..+6; diatonicArc(key) -> 12-bit mask plus arc-centre pc; classify(pc, key) -> 'diatonic' | 'flat-side' | 'sharp-side'.
2) A `maelstrom` module:
   - two 540x960 HalfFloat targets and a FullScreenQuad sim
   - uniforms: uPrev, uCenter, uR, uEye (rx, ry), uSpin, uZoom, uKeepIn, uKeepOut, uShock vec3
   - star data: uStars[STARS] vec4 (x px, y px, radius, energy) plus uStarLab
   - arc data: uArcs[STARS] vec4 (angle, half-width, radius, energy) plus uArcLab
   - STARS = 48 as a #define from one JS constant; pack into a 48x4 RGBA32F DataTexture if fragment uniform limits bite
   - a display quad in overlayScene
3) JS state: comets [{m, vel, t0, p0, p1, p2}], a wheelRot spring with hysteresis, a spin integrator, a root-motion arc queue.
4) The fixed 60 Hz sim step.
5) Scheme switching clears history and calls overlay.build() with the scheme's LAYOUT and lens shift.

RISKS:
- Rotate-plus-zoom resampling softens a little every step; fixed steps keep that refresh-independent. Add a 0.5 px unsharp tap only if it looks mushy.
- The key guess can jitter: hysteresis plus tau.
- Long names such as 'Dbmaj7#11' must shrink to fit the eye.
- Moving the label and staff changes a composition Daniel liked, so this ships as its own preset.

log_to_banter:
Moment cards: the moments that make the visuals flare become the questions the agents ask.

1) LOG. The page batches events to a new POST /api/piano-log (a sibling of /api/recordings), which appends to state/arsenal/piano-log/YYYYMMDD-HHMM.jsonl:
- note on/off: t, midi, vel
- pedal: t, raw CC64
- each settled chord change (when overlay.shown changes): t, chord name, voicing with octaves, bass, key guess and r, roughness, root motion in fifths, out-of-key pitch classes, and the REC file plus second if recording

2) FLAG. A pure Theory.flagMoment() marks three kinds of moment:
- a dark-side chord: a pitch class outside the rolling key, i.e. borrowed or secondary
- a roughness spike above 0.6 that resolves within two chords
- a root motion that is neither a fifth nor a step: a mediant or a tritone

Each flag becomes a card with 4 chords of context either side.

3) BANTER. After a session an agent picks one card and opens with a question, not a lecture. For example: 'At 3:42 you went Fmaj9 -> Fm6 -> Cmaj9. That Ab is borrowed from C minor, the minor iv. Did you reach for it on purpose, or did your hand find it?'

4) LEARN. Daniel's answer ('by ear', 'on purpose', 'no idea') is written back onto the card. Over weeks the cards add up to his habit fingerprint: favourite borrowed chords, which voicings he spreads, how he resolves tension. The agents can then banter from his own history: 'that's the minor iv again, always straight after the IV'.

The card's timestamp points at the second in the recorded video, and it is the same event that made the Maelstrom flare or the Plumes churn, so the TikTok moment and the theory conversation are the same thing.

angle: Minimal, elegant, cinematic. Colour and light only where they mean something; notation-grade typography; wide negative space. The current scheme is a light show. These two are a score you can watch. I read piano.js end to end and the r4 9:16 receipt. The wash-out has two causes. The first is visual: additive blending plus bloom plus the fifths hues on every tail. The second is harmonic: detect() runs over every sounding note, pedal-held ones included, so long pedalled passages also drift toward 'cluster' names. CC64 is already parsed (onMidiMessage feeds setSustain) and the trails already store press, release and sound-end times (aT0/aT1/aT2). So 'sustain-aware' is mostly a presentation job, plus one small helper, harmonySet(): the notes being held, plus pedal-held notes struck within the last 1.5 s. Both schemes share a small scheme switch. RenderPass.scene and .camera get swapped per scheme; bloom.strength, threshold and enabled are set per scheme; LAYOUT is keyed by scheme and then framing. Hooks go into noteOn, noteOff and setSustain, and the settle point in overlay.update where shown becomes pending. The 'stage' look stays exactly as it is. Neither scheme uses sparks, grain or time-varying dither: all motion comes from scrolling and eased values driven by uNow, so it looks identical at 60 Hz or 144 Hz. The recorder already paces capture to 60 fps.

schemes.name: Nocturne Roll
schemes.pitch: A slow, ink-black piano roll where every chord change writes its own lead-sheet symbol into the music as it rises, and pedalled notes become hairline ghosts instead of light.
schemes.visuals: LAYOUT 9:16 (1080x1920, y measured from the top). 0-230 is empty. The chord name has its baseline at y=380: Archivo 760, width 85, 132 px, INK ivory, no glow, just a 10 px shadow in rgba(1,2,6,0.6) for legibility. Below it at baseline 462, the note names in voicing order, 30 px, each coloured by its chord function (see colour). At baseline 506, a small-caps line such as 'V7 · C MAJOR': 24 px Archivo 600, letter-spacing 0.14em, ivory at 50%. The ROLL runs from y=560 to y=1330. It fades in from 560 to 680 (smoothstep alpha), so bars dissolve into the dark rather than hitting an edge. Scroll speed is a fixed 120 px/s, which shows 6.4 s of history. The HIT LINE at y=1330 is 2 px of ivory at 35%, with a 1 px soft edge. The KEY STRIP runs from 1336 to 1480 and is flat and 2D, not the lacquer model: white keys are 144 px tall in oklch(0.93 0.012 85); black keys are 90 px in #111317; 1 px gaps are ground colour. From 1480 to 1536 is a keybed hairline. Below 1536 nothing vital is drawn: only an optional 8% mirrored reflection of the key strip, fading out over 120 px. Horizontal framing reuses cam.x and cam.span from updateCamera, so the roll zooms slowly toward where the hands are (minSpan 16 gives about 67 px per white key), and historical bars rescale with it, which reads as a gentle push-in. The ground stays STAGE_DARK plus a static radial vignette that is 4% darker at the corners. The dither is a static Bayer pattern that never changes over time, so there is no crawl. NOTE BARS are rounded rectangles, 3 px corner radius, at 78% of the lane width for white keys and 56% for black. Normal blending, not additive. The held section is filled with the function colour at alpha 0.55 + 0.35*vel. Its top edge, which is the note-on moment, gets a 2 px attack line at L+0.08. NOTE-ON: the key fills with 35% of the function colour mixed into ivory, a 2 px coloured line lights on the key's top edge, and the hit line brightens to 70% over a 40 px span at that key, decaying with tau 0.18 s. This is the only element above the bloom threshold. No sparks. NOTE-OFF with the pedal up: the bar's lower end closes with its rounded corner and the key eases back, tau 0.12 s. NOTE-OFF with the pedal down: the bar continues as a hollow outline, a 1.5 px stroke in the same colour at alpha 0.5*exp(-tailAge/2.5 s) with a 0.05 interior fill, and the key keeps a 3 px coloured underline at its bottom edge meaning 'still ringing'. SUSTAIN PEDAL: a pedal lane at x=28 (the left gutter, clear of TikTok's right-side button rail). It is a 2 px ivory line at 55% that scrolls exactly like a note while the pedal is down. Each pedal-down draws an 8 px horizontal notch plus a 'Ped.' label in 16 px Archivo 500 small caps at 40%. A quick re-pedal draws the classic notch, so legato pedalling becomes readable like a score. CHORD CHANGE, at the existing 120/300 ms settle point: stamp a CHORD MARKER, a 1.5 px hairline across the roll at 14% ivory that scrolls up with the music. At its left end (x=44) a dark pill (rgba(1,2,6,0.72), 6 px radius) holds the chord symbol in 30 px Archivo 600 at 85% ivory, with the scale degree in 20 px at 45% beside it. The roll becomes a lead sheet you can freeze-frame. The big chord name crossfades: the old one fades out over 140 ms while the new one rises 8 px into place (tau 0.12). The scale pop is dropped. COLOUR (the new 'function' mode, the default in this scheme; the existing colour-select still offers pitch, velocity and amber): root = gold oklch(0.86 0.11 85); 3rd and 7th (guide tones) = teal oklch(0.80 0.10 195); 5th = ivory oklch(0.90 0.02 85); 9th, 11th, 13th and altered tones = lavender oklch(0.78 0.10 295); notes outside the named chord = grey oklch(0.68 0 0). A fresh note starts ivory and settles into its function colour over 0.22 s, measured by time along the bar, so a rolled chord develops like a photograph. If a note is still sounding when its function changes (a common tone), the bar splits into a continuation segment with flat joining ends. The history stays honest: you can watch the G that was the 5th of C become the root of G. 16:9 (1920x1080): roll from y=190 to 880, keys 886-1000, chord name top-left at x=80 with baseline 150, pedal lane at x=40, markers on the left.
schemes.theory_value: It shows harmonic rhythm: the marker lines show how long each chord lasts and where changes land against the pedal. It teaches voicing: gold, teal and lavender make it visible that the 3rd and 7th define the chord's quality, and that his lush sound comes from lavender extensions stacked over a thin root. Common tones visibly change their job at chord boundaries, which is the core idea of smooth voice-leading. The degree line ('ii · V7 · I in C major', via a new pure Theory.degreeOf) turns chord names into function. The pedal lane shows whether he pedals legato (lifting just after the change) or rides the pedal across changes. That blur is exactly the wash he saw, and now he can see it rather than lose the picture to it.
schemes.tiktok_value: It reads as premium the moment you see it: black ground, ivory type, colour used sparingly. Chord symbols scrolling up are a pause-and-read hook ('what's that chord at 0:07'), and the comments do the teaching for him. It screenshots cleanly into a thumbnail with a legible chord name. There is no glare to smear under TikTok's H.264 re-encode, since hairlines and flat fills compress far better than bloom walls. Vital elements sit between y=250 and 1480, and gutter labels sit on the left, away from the right-side button rail.
schemes.sustain_behaviour: Held = filled bar, pedal-sustained = hollow outline with a 5% fill and exponential fade, and blending is normal rather than additive. Twenty overlapping pedalled notes therefore make a fine lattice of coloured hairlines, never a white slab: the brightest a pixel can get is one outline's colour. The pedal lane makes the pedal itself a readable object instead of an implied glow. Function colour and chord markers read from harmonySet(): held notes plus pedal-held notes struck within the last 1.5 s. So riding the pedal across three chords still names the new chord, and older ringing notes go grey. Key underlines show which strings are still ringing without adding light.
schemes.build_sketch: Reuses: keyX, the cam.x/cam.span follow math, noteLch/oklchToLinear (port the OKLab-to-linear matrix into GLSL for the colour ease), the trails instanced-quad pattern with the aT0/aT1/aT2 timing model, makeLayer/nameRuns/drawRuns and the INK and FONT constants, Theory.detect/estimateKey, overlay's settle logic, setSustain, and the composer, with bloom set to strength 0.15 and threshold 0.92. New code: (1) A scheme switch (~40 lines): SCHEMES.stage/roll/orbit, each with build, dispose, onNoteOn, onNoteOff, onSustain, onChord and update; renderPass.scene and .camera are swapped, and overlay.staff.mesh.visible is false for this scheme. (2) rollScene with an OrthographicCamera using a non-uniform frustum: x in key units from cam.x-span/2 to cam.x+span/2, y in output pixels. Scroll speed then never changes with zoom, and the fragment shader gets a uPxPerKey uniform for pixel-true rounded corners and strokes. (3) makeLanes({max:640, speedPx:120, goneAfterPx:900}), a parameterised copy of trails with extra attributes aLabFrom (vec3), aLabTo (vec3), aColT and aFlags (bit0 = continuation, which means no attack line and flat ends). Fragment shader: time at this pixel is uNow - (hitY - y)/speed. Colour = OKLab mix(from, to, smoothstep(aColT, aColT+0.22, that time)). Held, tail and outline come from sdRoundBox with fwidth antialiasing. (4) The flat key strip: 88 instanced quads with aDown, aTint and aRing attributes, updated only on events. (5) The pedal lane: a second makeLanes ring of 64 slots. Pedal-down and pedal-up map to T0 and T2. 'Ped.' labels are sprites. (6) Chord markers: a ring of 16 small 420x64 CanvasTexture sprites, drawn once when created, with y positions set in a CPU loop each frame (16 writes). (7) Pure THEORY additions, node-tested: degreeOf(rootPc, suffix, key) returns a roman numeral. Case comes from quality, with ° for dim and ø for m7b5. Flats are relative to the tonic (bVII, bVI). The minor key's rows are separate. functionOf(note, info) derives root, 3rd, 5th, 7th or extension from letter steps (steps 0/2/4/6, with dim7's step-5 7th counted as a 7th). Also harmonySet(sounding, t). Roughly 550 new lines. Risks: 1.5 px hairlines that scroll by subpixel amounts can twinkle in H.264. Keep strokes at 1.5 px or more with a soft fwidth edge, and snap marker text sprites to whole pixels. Continuation segments must not use up the 640-slot cap in very long pedalled pieces; recycle any lane more than 900 px past the hit line. Re-running detection on the settle hook must stay throttled, which the existing detectDirty flag already covers.

schemes.name: Orbit
schemes.pitch: All 88 keys fold into a single circle of fifths, so every chord you play draws its own shape. Every major chord is the same triangle turned, a dominant seventh carries a line of tension straight through the centre, and borrowed chords light up outside the key.
schemes.visuals: LAYOUT 9:16 (y from the top). 0-230 is empty. The chord name has its baseline at 360: 128 px Archivo 760, ivory, centred. The degree and key line has its baseline at 425: 26 px small caps at 50%, e.g. 'bVII · C MAJOR (BORROWED)'. The RING is centred at (540, 880) with radius 285: a 1.5 px ivory hairline at 12%. Twelve stations sit in circle-of-fifths order, C at 12 o'clock, then G, D, A clockwise. This is the same order the existing hue wheel uses, so each station's colour is its noteColor hue. Station ticks are 14 px radial marks at 22%. Letters sit at r=335: 26 px Archivo 500, ivory at 40%, spelled from the key guess (Db rather than C# in flat keys). The KEY WINDOW is a 3 px arc at r=305, ivory at 30%, spanning the key's 7 diatonic stations (always contiguous on the fifths circle) with ±12° of overhang. A 6 px solid dot marks the tonic station. When the key estimate changes, the arc rotates the short way round, tau 0.6 s. Below the ring, at baseline 1262, is the PROGRESSION LINE. The current chord symbol is centred at x=540 (30 px, 90%) with its roman numeral under it (20 px, 45%). The four previous chords sit to the left at 190 px spacing, fading to 55%, 30%, 15% and 6%. The right side stays empty on purpose: that is where the future goes, and it keeps clear of TikTok's button rail. The KEY STRIP runs from 1330 to 1480: the same flat 88-key strip as Nocturne Roll, following cam.x and cam.span. NOTE-ON: the key lights. A filament rises from the key's top edge to its pitch-class station: a quadratic curve with its control point at (keyX, 1120), 1.5 px wide, in the pitch hue. A bright pulse travels along it in 300 ms and the thread then fades over 500 ms. You see all the octaves of C collapse onto one point. The station node blooms on: a disc of radius 16+8*vel/127, filled with the pitch hue, eased in with tau 60 ms. It is the only element above the bloom threshold (strength 0.3, threshold 0.8). Doubled octaves of the same pitch class add concentric 1.5 px rings at +7 px each, up to 3. NOTE-OFF with the pedal up: the node shrinks and fades, tau 180 ms. NOTE-OFF with the pedal down: the node becomes a 2 px outline ring in its hue, alpha 0.8*exp(-age/3 s) with a floor of 0.3. SUSTAIN PEDAL: the ring hairline thickens from 1.5 to 2.5 px and warms from 12% ivory to 20% oklch(0.85 0.05 80) while the pedal is down (tau 0.15 s). The pedal is felt as the room holding its breath, not as added brightness. THE SHAPE: the stations in harmonySet() are joined in circle order by 2 px ivory edges at 70%, and the interior is filled with glowMix (the average chord colour, already computed in renderFrame) at 7%. The bass note (lowest MIDI note) gets a thin spoke from the ring centre to its station at 35%. So C/E shows the C triangle with the spoke on E. Any two sounding pitch classes that are 6 stations apart (a tritone) get their edge drawn as a diameter in warm amber oklch(0.82 0.12 70): the tension line. CHORD CHANGE, at the settle hook: the old shape is snapshotted, scales 1.00 to 1.04 and fades to 0 over 0.5 s, a single ghost that is never stacked. The new shape's edges draw on with stroke progress 0 to 1 over 180 ms. The progression line slides left one slot, tau 0.25 s. The chord name crossfades with an 8 px rise, as in Nocturne Roll. Stations outside the key window glow with a 1 px amber ring, so borrowed or chromatic notes are unmistakable. 16:9: ring centred at (620, 500) with r=300; chord name, degree and a vertical progression column on the right at x=1120-1800; keys across y=900-1040; filaments rise to the ring at the left.
schemes.theory_value: It is the most direct theory lesson a visual can give. Chord QUALITY is SHAPE: every major triad is the same triangle rotated, minor is its mirror, a dominant 7th is that triangle plus a diameter, and diminished 7ths are squares. TRANSPOSITION is ROTATION. The KEY is an arc of 7 neighbours, and diatonic progressions (ii-V-I) walk anticlockwise around it. Borrowed chords (bVII, iv in major, the Picardy third) show up as nodes outside the arc, so the 'why does this sound special' moment gets named on screen: 'bVII · BORROWED'. The bass spoke explains inversions and slash chords. The octave-collapse filaments teach pitch class versus pitch, the idea detection already relies on internally. The progression line with numerals shows his habits as function rather than letters, which carries across every key he plays in.
schemes.tiktok_value: It is instantly shareable geometry: 'your favourite chord is a shape' is an education hook that works with the sound off, and the draw-on of a new shape on each change is satisfying. A clean centred composition screenshots as a poster. It can loop: the ring never runs out of room. It is very kind to compression (sparse lines, one bloom source per note). It is distinct from every falling-notes video in the feed, and it pairs with Nocturne Roll as a series: 'same take, two lenses'.
schemes.sustain_behaviour: It cannot wash out by construction: there are only 12 stations, so the brightest possible frame is 12 discs. Pedal-held notes become outline rings that decay to a 30% floor while the pedal is down. That keeps ringing notes and struck notes readable without any additive build-up. The shape uses harmonySet() (held notes plus pedal-held notes struck within the last 1.5 s), so a pedal ridden across a progression still draws each new chord cleanly, while older ringing pitch classes keep their hollow rings but lose their edges. Lifting the pedal clears the hollow rings with tau 180 ms, a visible 'breath' matching the pedal change. The ring hairline's warmth marks pedal state without adding any light near the shape.
schemes.build_sketch: Reuses: noteColor and noteCss (the fifths hue already matches the ring positions), keyX with cam follow for the key strip (shared with Nocturne Roll), Theory.detect/estimateKey, the degreeOf/harmonySet/functionOf helpers from Nocturne Roll, glowMix, overlay makeLayer/nameRuns/drawRuns for the chord name and progression line (redrawn only on change), the settle hook, the composer with bloom retuned, and setSustain. New code: (1) orbitScene with OrthographicCamera(0,1080,1920,0) in pixel space, used via the scheme switch. (2) ONE ring quad (760x760) with an SDF fragment shader. Uniform arrays: uNode[12] as vec4 (level, held, pedalAge, octaves), uNodeCol[12] as vec3, uEdge[12] as vec4 segment endpoints plus uEdgeKind[12] (0 = normal, 1 = tritone, 2 = sustain-weak), uEdgeProg (draw-on), uBass as vec2, uArc as vec3 (start angle, length, tonic angle), uPedal, uGhost (an 8-vertex polygon plus alpha/scale, or a second pass of the same shader). Hairlines use sdSegment and sdCircle with fwidth antialiasing. The interior fill is an even-odd crossing test over the edge array in the shader, or a small triangle-fan Mesh rebuilt on chord change (preferred: cheaper and simpler). Per-frame CPU cost is about 40 uniform writes. (3) Filaments: an instanced 32-segment ribbon, up to 48 instances. The vertex shader evaluates the quadratic curve from aKeyX, aStation and aT0. The pulse position is smoothstep(aT0, aT0+0.3, uNow), and alpha decays after that. Key x in pixels comes from the strip's projection, so filaments follow the camera zoom. (4) Station letters: a single CanvasTexture ring layer, redrawn only when the key-guess spelling bias flips. (5) Pure THEORY, node-tested: fifthsStation(pc) = pc*7 mod 12; keyWindow(key) = 7 pitch classes, the relative major's F-to-B arc rotated; isBorrowed(info, key). Roughly 500 new lines, about 350 if Nocturne Roll's key strip, scheme switch and theory helpers land first. Risks: estimateKey's pitch-class history decays with tau 12 s, so the arc can wobble during chromatic passages. Add hysteresis (a new key needs r at least 0.05 better for 2 s) before rotating.
